items.title: Being locally of finite type is fpqc local on the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property 'f is locally of finite type' is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 5953-5957). The proof follows the same pattern as its finite-presentation sibling: base-change stability and Zariski locality are recorded, the situation is reduced to a flat surjective morphism of affines and an affine open U of X, the rings S = Spec(R), S' = Spec(R'), U = Spec(A), U' = Spec(A') are named with R -> R' faithfully flat, A' = R' tensor_R A and R' -> A' of finite type, and the algebra descent lemma for finite type yields that R -> A is of finite type; the general locality lemma concludes (proof lines 5959-5980). The level is H2: the card is short, but the reduction and the ring-theoretic input are both explicit.
